title: "The Day the Pride Won": OU's Band and the 1983 Bedlam Comeback
question: What was The Day the Pride Won in Oklahoma football history?
answer: "The Day the Pride Won" was Oklahoma's 21-20 comeback at Oklahoma State on October 15, 1983, when the Pride of Oklahoma band kept playing "Boomer Sooner" as OU rallied from 20-3 down. Barry Switzer gave the band an honorary game ball.
summary: On Oct. 15, 1983, OU rallied from 20-3 to win at Oklahoma State 21-20 while the band played Boomer Sooner nonstop. Switzer gave the band an honorary game ball.
body: Most game balls go to players. One of the most famous in Sooner history went to a marching band. On October 15, 1983, No. 15 Oklahoma visited Oklahoma State at Lewis Field in Stillwater and found itself in deep trouble, trailing 20-3 early in the fourth quarter.

According to band lore, the Pride of Oklahoma responded by playing "Boomer Sooner" without stopping, an estimated 300 times over the course of the comeback, with director Gene Thrailkill telling the band to keep going. Whether or not the exact count holds up, the music never quit, and neither did the Sooners.

The fourth quarter belonged to Oklahoma. Danny Bradley hit Derrick Shepard for a 73-yard touchdown, Spencer Tillman ran in a 5-yard score with a successful two-point conversion, and Tim Lashar finished it with a 46-yard field goal with 1:14 left. OU scored 18 points in the period and escaped with a 21-20 win.

Coach Barry Switzer credited the band, and the honor came to be known by the label "The Day the Pride Won." The band's prize was an honorary one, a 5x7 glossy photo of the game ball. It stood as the band's last game-ball honor until 2015, when the athletic department gave members actual game balls after a double-overtime win at Tennessee. Fittingly, Pride director Brian Britt had been a freshman in that 1983 band.
